what: How far each kind of hand skin may sink into a held object before it counts as a press past its give (cm). Measured values come from the sources below; the rest are still guesses and are marked so.

palm.citation: Spartacus V, Shojaeizadeh M, Raffault V, Shoults J, Van Wieren K, Sparrey CJ. In vivo soft tissue compressive properties of the human hand. PLOS ONE 16(12): e0261008 (2021). doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0261008
palm.data: Supplementary S4 Table: the depth pressed in at 31% of the soft tissue's thickness over the trapezium, 15 adults, wrist at 0 degrees, 0.2 Hz: mean 2.72 mm, SD 0.45, range 1.92 to 3.35 (women 2.40, men 3.01); the force there 1.02 N on a 3 mm flat indenter, about 144 kPa. Supplementary S3 Table: stiffness 0.26 N/mm (small deformation) and 0.54 N/mm (large).
palm.reading: The column headed '31 % of thickness' is read as the depth pressed in (mm): the forces and the stiffness agree only with that reading. That reading is ours, not the paper's statement.
palm.applied_as: The palm's sink at grip pressure: published palm pressures in a grip are about 100 to 250 kPa, and 144 kPa is inside that range.
palm.limits: Measured over the thumb's base (the trapezium), not over the index and middle metacarpals; a 3 mm indenter sinks further than a broad grip surface at the same pressure, so the value is likely a little high.

pad.citation: Dzidek BM, Adams MJ, Andrews JW, Zhang Z, Johnson SA. Contact mechanics of the human finger pad under compressive loads. J. R. Soc. Interface 14: 20160935 (2017). doi:10.1098/rsif.2016.0935
pad.data: An index finger pad pressed on flat glass: 'The maximum displacement was ~ 1.6 mm', at a normal force of 2 N.
pad.support: Serina ER, Mote CD, Rempel D. Force response of the fingertip pulp to repeated compression: effects of loading rate, loading angle and anthropometry. J Biomech 30: 1035-1040 (1997): the pulp is compliant below 1 N and stiffens fast above it.
pad.limits: One subject (female, 27, left index finger), up to 2 N.
